Shri Manish Dutt, Sr. Advocate with Shri Ashish Tiwar
 the applicant.
Shri Vinod Tiwari-P.L. for the State.

Order 
This is the second bail application filed by present applicant under Section 483 of the BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.319 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Dehat,
District-Tikamgarh, for the offence punishable under sections 420, 419, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of IPC.

2. Prosecution story, in brief, is that co-accused Farasram @ Farshi Kewat impersonated as Ramdayal Ahirwar, original owner of the property and executed sale deed in favour of Krishna Kant Agrawal for a consideration of Rs.12 lacs in the year 2023 and co-accused person along with another person Amit Shrivastava had signed as an attesting witnesses whereas applicant Dinesh facilitated the same as broker.
3.
Learned Senior counsel for applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 7.10.2024 and material witnesses have been examined.
Krishna Kant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12282 2 MCRC-55141-2024
Agrawal in his statement has clearly stated that at the time of execution of sale deed, present applicant was not present and he had seen applicant for the first time.
It is also urged that present applicant is ready to deposit sale consideration as mentioned in the sale deed.
On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned P.L. for the respondent/State on the other hand has opposed the application.

5. Having regard to the facts of the case and also looking to the submissions of learned counsel for the applicant that he will deposit sale consideration of Rs.12 lacs before the trial Court, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that present applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial and also that he will deposit Rs.12 lacs before the Trial Court.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
8. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
